prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the development of long-acting incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: The first round showed that all six of us regard the GLP-1 chain as mature and independently replicated, so the only live question is what the citation says the prize is for. I hold that the physiology and the medicine are one achievement: proglucagon processing, the incretin effect and the active truncated peptide (Holst), receptor and tissue biology with the therapeutic logic (Drucker), and the molecular design that gave the hormone a long enough half-life to be used as a drug (Knudsen). Acylation to bind albumin and resist DPP-4 degradation is a designed solution to a specific biochemical obstacle, and without it the physiology would not have reached patients or produced the outcome-trial evidence we all cite. A citation that names both the discovery and the development is accurate to what happened and fits the mandate. I also keep the configuration as a single part. A second part under the three-person cap would force one of the GLP-1 names out, and I do not think B006 or B021 is strong enough relative to B005 this year to justify that cost.
statement.case_against: The strongest argument against my configuration is the one raised by Perlmann, Svenningsson, El Manira and Wahren-Herlenius: the Nobel Prize has rewarded discovery far more often than industrial optimisation, and a discovery-only trio with Mojsov is a legitimate and tidier reading. Four members prefer it. My trio also leaves out Mojsov, whose identification and synthesis of the active peptide is a real contribution, and Habener and other early contributors are outside every configuration the cap allows. I cannot settle Mojsov's priority from the file, and my account of the GLP-1 history is partly from recollection. If the committee's majority wants the citation on discovery alone, mine is the minority configuration and could look like a prize for a product.

responses.point: The chair argues that Drucker, Holst and Mojsov already capture the arc, that the Knudsen and Mojsov trios differ in what they say the Nobel is for, and that industrial drug development is a separate story from the discovery.
responses.response: I accept the point that the two trios make different statements, and that is exactly the decision before us. I do not accept that the discovery trio already covers the arc. Neither Holst nor Drucker designed a molecule with a once-weekly profile, and the citation cannot say the therapies followed from the discovery unless someone credited did the design work. I would also note that the trio you propose still rests on a priority question you and others cannot resolve from the file, whereas Knudsen's role in liraglutide and semaglutide is not disputed. Your question on whether I would accept a discovery-only citation: I would, but only if it is narrowed to physiology and peptide identification and no longer says 'enabled treatment'. If the committee goes that way, I will vote for the Mojsov trio as a defensible second choice and will not treat it as an error.

responses.point: Perlmann prefers the discovery trio with Mojsov because it credits the discovery of the hormone's active form most cleanly, and now ranks B006 ahead of B021 because the CAR-T credit problem is unresolved.
responses.response: On B005 we will probably remain apart, but you have changed my view on the alternatives. Your argument that the CAR-T credit gap around Eshhar cannot be repaired by choosing among the credited names is correct, and I weighed it too lightly in round 1. I now put B006 ahead of B021 as my first alternative. I still disagree that Knudsen's acylated analogues are only industrial optimisation. The design addressed a defined mechanism of clearance and binding, which is original medicinal chemistry, and your own file calls them the molecules that reached patients.

responses.point: El Manira prefers Drucker, Holst and Mojsov because they fit a discovery citation within three names, says a Knudsen variant is defensible, and favours the June and Sadelain pair over the three-person CAR-T credit.
responses.response: Thank you for saying a Knudsen variant is defensible, since the chair's summary suggests the choice may come down to which risk the committee prefers. On CAR-T I agree with you and with Linnarsson that June and Sadelain is cleaner. I held Rosenberg in round 1 as the conceptual base, but his work on adoptive transfer and TIL therapy is partly distinct, and I no longer think that justifies the third name. Your point that B006 is stronger on conceptual originality also persuades me to rank it first among alternatives. The cost is the same under the cap: any second part removes a GLP-1 laureate, and I would not accept that cost for either alternative this year.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius sees CAR-T as a very good candidate for a later year, because long-term toxicity and secondary malignancy are still being characterised and the Eshhar gap makes the three-name credit insecure.
responses.response: I agree, and the toxicity point strengthens it. Secondary T-cell malignancy and late neurological events are still being documented, and the autoimmunity extension is not yet established, so a CAR-T prize would be on firmer ground in a few years with a settled credit. You said you would not object strongly to a Knudsen variant if Mojsov's priority proved too uncertain. I would add that the committee does not need to rule on Mojsov versus Habener to produce a defensible prize, since a configuration without Mojsov does not require the priority dispute to be resolved. Where I disagree is your concern that omitting the drug design looks incomplete. I think it is incomplete, and that is a reason to include Knudsen.

responses.point: Linnarsson argues that a single citation spanning physiology and drug design is the better design, and that B006 is the cleaner configuration if the committee cannot settle the GLP-1 third name.
responses.response: I agree on both points. A second part cannot carry the drug design without dropping a laureate, so the citation has to state the chain. Your point that B006 becomes preferable if attribution fails is the one I keep returning to. I would not move to B006 on the Mojsov question alone, because that question does not make B005 unsafe: both trios are defensible and the committee can decide between them on principle. I would move to B006 only if the committee judged that no GLP-1 trio could be credited without leaving a clearly deserving person out. I do not think that threshold is met.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's contribution to identifying the active peptide should outweigh Knudsen's design of the long-acting analogues, given that Habener is outside the credited names and I cannot verify the priority history from the file.
Whether the committee will accept a citation that includes drug development; if the majority prefers discovery only, my configuration is in the minority and I would move to the narrowed Mojsov trio.
Whether the B006 mechanism, with an indirect disease link, should outweigh the cost of any two-part prize on the three-person cap.
Part of my account of the GLP-1 and CAR-T history rests on recollection and not on documents in the shortlist.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any credited name on the shortlist. I disclose co-authorship with Sten Linnarsson (about eight joint works, count not audited) and with Jonas Frisen, and earlier work in Christopher Burge's group at MIT. None of these people is credited on any shortlisted ballot, and shared Karolinska Institutet affiliation does not establish a conflict. I request no recusal.
